correctness.rationale: The four partial derivatives have no common projective zero. Every line has one unique RREF chart; all six chart coefficient lists were independently verified as polynomial identities by checker.py. The two nonempty 27-line charts reduce to separable additive degree-nine polynomials, with all nonzero roots in exact Frobenius eight-cycles. Four additional prime-field lines account for 58 geometric lines. The normal bundle O(-2) on each line proves the finite Hilbert scheme is reduced and étale. The zeta function and all-extension line counts follow from the Galois cycle type. A standalone checker was replayed from its actual prepared package path; no computation is used as an infinite-field substitute.

originality.rationale: Veniani (arXiv:1608.04209, Example 5.1) establishes the one-parameter geometric 58-line family but does not record its prime-field Frobenius cycle decomposition. Degtyarev (arXiv:1604.05836, Theorem 1.2 and Section 8.4) classifies geometric configurations, not Frobenius actions on the 58-line scheme. Rams-Schütt (arXiv:1409.7485, Example 2.1) provides the 112-line Fermat quartic over F9, a different surface and splitting behavior. The new exact 1^10 8^6 cycle type, degree-eight minimal splitting extension, and zero-dimensional zeta function do not follow merely from the published geometric total of 58 lines.
residual_risks: An unlocated number-theoretic or finite-field computation of this same K3 model could contain the cycle decomposition even though the identified geometric references do not.

value.rationale: The exact arithmetic of lines on a prominent maximal non-Fermat 58-line K3 quartic is motivated by Galois descent of extremal line configurations, an intrinsic question not resolved by their geometric classification. The complete finite-étale zeta function and unexpectedly large minimal splitting field F_{3^8} are natural exact arithmetic invariants useful for finite-field searches and incidence geometry. The fixed coefficient-one member is the nonzero prime-field specialization of Veniani’s natural one-parameter family, not an arbitrary constructed slice. No claim to a general family theorem is made.
